source_name: Česká leasingová a finanční asociace (ČLFA) — Členské společnosti
why_relevant: ČLFA is the Czech leasing and consumer-finance association; its member-company page is the standard enumeration of leasing companies, non-bank consumer lenders and factoring providers operating in CZ — the segment that sits outside the bank list but competes directly with bank lending. Essential complement to the ČBA roster for full coverage of Czech credit provision.

source_name: ČLFA — Statistiky / Informace o trhu (leasing, non-bank credit, factoring)
why_relevant: ČLFA publishes quarterly and annual market statistics for leasing, non-bank consumer credit and factoring, with a dedicated ČLFA series covering 2016-2026 and an English-language 'Quarterly and yearly results of leasing, non-bank credit and factoring markets in the Czech Republic' mirror. It additionally republishes Leaseurope and Eurofinas European statistics, which lets you benchmark CZ against EU peers without paying either federation. Half-year 2026 data was already posted at time of scouting.

source_name: Asociace factoringových společností ČR (AFS ČR) — factoring statistics, hosted by ČLFA
why_relevant: A distinct sector association — the Czech factoring companies' association — whose quarterly and annual factoring market statistics are published through the ČLFA site. Observed series run at least 2023-2026 with quarterly granularity (1. čtvrtletí / 1. pololetí / 1.-3. čtvrtletí / rok). Factoring turnover is a leading indicator of SME working-capital stress and of bank-vs-non-bank share shift, and this is the only free consolidated Czech factoring series found.

source_name: ČLFA — Tiskové zprávy, výroční zprávy a stanoviska
why_relevant: ČLFA's press area is unusually productive and current — four press releases dated July-August 2026 were linked directly from the homepage, covering half-year results, consumer credit, electric-vehicle financing and Eurofinas Q1 comparisons. The site also carries annual reports (cs and an 'annual-report' English variant), plus 'Stanoviska ČLFA' position papers that reveal the association's regulatory lobbying agenda — a good early-warning channel for legislation affecting non-bank credit.

source_name: Česká fintech asociace / Czech Fintech Association (ČEFTAS) — Členové
why_relevant: ČEFTAS (founded 2016) is the Czech fintech industry body. Its members page distinguishes 'řádní členové' (full members offering fintech solutions) from 'přidružení členové' (ecosystem supporters), and also lists partner organisations and media/conference partners — three separate enumerations in one page. This is the primary map of the Czech fintech actor set, which is otherwise poorly covered by bank-centric registries. Leadership observed to include executives from Twisto, EasyChange Group and Budget Bakers; the association itself is a member of AMSP ČR, the Czech Chamber of Commerce and the European Digital Finance Association.

source_name: ČEFTAS — Články (curated fintech news stream)
why_relevant: In contrast to the association's own stale press-release category, the /clanky/ stream is actively maintained (items observed dated 14-20 August 2026) and mixes Czech-language commentary with curated international fintech news, syndicating from fintree.cz, TechCrunch and similar. Valuable less as primary evidence than as a signal of what the Czech fintech establishment considers important, and as a pointer to Czech fintech media outlets (fintree.cz, ctit.cz podcasts) worth adding to the source map.

source_name: Asociace pro elektronickou komerci (APEK) — Seznam členů
why_relevant: APEK's member directory explicitly states 570 listed members across 64 paginated pages, each with its own detail URL. This is by a wide margin the largest single enumeration found in this cell and the definitive map of the Czech e-commerce merchant and vendor base — the demand side for acquiring, payment gateways, BNPL and POS services. Each member detail page is a stable per-company URL, making the directory usable as a persistent company registry, not just a list.

source_name: APEKdata — Czech e-commerce statistics portal (incl. payments)
why_relevant: APEK's dedicated data property, tracking e-commerce turnover in CZK bn, share of total retail (stated at over ten percent), employment, delivery, purchase frequency and device mix — and, directly relevant to this run, a dedicated 'Platby' (Payments) section on how Czech consumers pay online. Sourced from APEK plus Heureka. This is the best free demand-side payments-mix dataset for CZ and complements SBK's issuer-side card statistics from the opposite direction. Note the site cites 'more than 650' APEK members versus 570 listed on the directory — reconcile before quoting either figure.

source_name: APEK — Pro novináře / Novinky a tiskové zprávy
why_relevant: APEK's press channel, with a named press contact (executive director Jan Vetyška) and a running news feed covering Czech e-commerce regulation — e.g. an item on parliament deciding parcel-locker installations will not fall under the building code. APEK is an active lobbying voice on retail payments and consumer-protection legislation, so this feed is an early indicator of rule changes affecting online payment acceptance.

source_name: Komunita APEK — member community, studies and legal documents
why_relevant: APEK runs a Discourse-based community carrying APEK studies (/s/apek-studie/), legal documents (/s/pravni-dokumenty/) and webinar archives (/c/apek-webinare/). Association-commissioned studies on Czech online shopping and payment behaviour are exactly the kind of grey literature that never surfaces in search engines, making this a high-value but hard-to-reach tier.

source_name: Asociace pro kapitálový trh ČR (AKAT) — Členové asociace
why_relevant: AKAT is the Czech capital-market/asset-management association, splitting its roster into 'Řádní členové' and 'Přidružení členové'. Its own press release notes the association passed 100 members and marked 30 years. Members are the asset managers, fund distributors and custodians attached to Czech banking groups (most large Czech banks run a captive investment company), so this roster completes the picture of bank-affiliated entities that publish their own disclosures.

source_name: AKAT — Zveřejněná data (fund and asset-management data series)
why_relevant: AKAT's structured data programme, publishing member-submitted series on a defined schedule with codified report types — daily data (IP 1, net asset value per unit; noted as discontinued from 1.9.2020) and monthly data (IP 2, assets under management), governed by a binding instruction ('aktuální závazný pokyn'). The page explicitly warns that figures cover association members only. Complemented by a 'Historická data' archive. This is a genuine recurring dataset rather than a press page.

source_name: AKAT — Tiskové zprávy a výroční zprávy
why_relevant: AKAT issues quarterly press releases with headline market aggregates — observed examples report Czech investments passing the four-trillion-CZK mark (Q2, 17 Aug 2026) and the count of Long-Term Investment Product (DIP) contracts opened rising to 265,829 (30 Jul 2026). DIP uptake is a direct read on how successfully Czech banks are converting deposit balances into investment products, which is squarely an A1 earnings-narrative input. The annual report archive runs back to 2014/2015 with an RSS feed available.

source_name: Asociace českých stavebních spořitelen (AČSS)
why_relevant: Snowballed extension to the cell: the association of Czech building societies (stavební spořitelny), all of which are bank subsidiaries of the major groups (Modrá pyramida/KB, ČSOB Stavební spořitelna, Raiffeisen stavební spořitelna, Stavební spořitelna ČS). Site carries 'Členové AČSS', 'Orgány AČSS', a 'Čísla a grafy' statistics section, a 'Novináři a odborníci' press area, legislation tracking and a terminology glossary. Building-society deposits and loans are a material and separately-regulated slice of Czech retail banking that the ČBA roster alone under-represents. Note acss.cz redirects to stavebnisporitelny.cz.

source_name: Česká asociace společností finančního poradenství a zprostředkování (ČASF)
why_relevant: Snowballed extension: the association of Czech financial advisory and intermediation companies — the distribution layer through which a large share of Czech mortgages, consumer credit and investment products is actually sold. Site carries 'Členské společnosti' (member companies), 'Finančně poradenský trh' (market data on the advisory sector), an ethics committee, and a media section. Member of FECIF at European level. Important for understanding origination channels that banks depend on but do not own. Note usfcr.cz redirects here, indicating an earlier identity (USF ČR) — useful for historical archive searches.

source_name: Česká asociace pojišťoven (ČAP)
why_relevant: The Czech insurance association, relevant to this cell because bancassurance is a significant fee-income line for every large Czech bank and most banking groups own or distribute for an insurer. Its member registry and statistics would complete the financial-sector association map. Recorded here as a HYPOTHESIS: the connection was reset on fetch, which typically indicates bot defence rather than a dead site — liveness must be confirmed by the deterministic verification pass.

source_name: ČEFTAS Visualbook — association brand and identity assets
why_relevant: The Czech Fintech Association's brand portal, serving logos, typography and colour specifications in CZ/SK/EN. Marginal for market intelligence, but it confirms the ČEFTAS acronym and the association's Czech/Slovak dual-market positioning, and it is the kind of asset that dates rebrands — useful when reconciling historical references to the association under different names.

source_name: Protext advanced search (vyhledávání) – full wire archive query interface
why_relevant: Query interface over the whole Protext archive. Observed filters: free text (Hledaný text), date range (Datum od / Datum do), origin (vše / ČR / zahraničí) and release language (vše / čeština / angličtina). The page reported 50,525 records found for the unfiltered query, with page-numbered pagination. This is the practical harvesting entry point for keyword sweeps such as 'banka', 'platební', 'platební instituce', 'karty', 'terminál'.

source_name: Protext submission/client portal (protext.ctk.cz)
why_relevant: The client-facing side of the ČTK wire. Documents how Czech corporate announcements physically enter the media system: service running since 1999, distribution to 27 Czech news portals and media in nearly 180 countries, guaranteed publication within 4 hours (usually under 2), category targeting, premium portal placement, and monitoring reports at 2h and 48h after publication. Registration is free and one-off submission without registration is possible — which explains why very small payment institutions and fintechs appear on the wire without any newsroom of their own. Useful for modelling distribution latency and for enumerating the downstream mirror portals.

source_name: České noviny – PR servis (ČTK/Protext mirror)
why_relevant: ČTK's own consumer news site mirrors the Protext PR feed in a dedicated /pr/ section. Confirmed on fetch: items dated (Aug 2026 range), a 'Všechny zprávy' loader, and financial-sector releases present (KB+ client-numbers release). Individual items follow the pattern /tiskove/zpravy/<slug>/<numeric-id>, which gives stable, citable permalinks with a numeric identifier — often easier to key on than the company's own CMS URLs. Acts as a redundant copy if protext.cz blocks automated access.

source_name: České noviny – Ekonomika (ČTK economic wire; successor of financninoviny.cz)
why_relevant: ČTK's edited economic news stream, where wire journalists rewrite or amplify bank and payment-company announcements. Important as the editorial counterpart to the raw PR feed: an item appearing here (rather than only in /pr/) signals that ČTK judged it newsworthy, which is a useful salience filter. Note the former dedicated finance domain financninoviny.cz now 301-redirects here, so legacy links and bookmarks resolve to this path.

source_name: ČTK services hub (Infobanka, ČTK Connect, News Select, Fotobanka)
why_relevant: Catalogue of the national agency's commercial products, which is where the deep, licensable archive lives: Infobanka (news database and archive), ČTK Connect (PR distribution and events), News Select (mobile news app), PressCentrum ČTK (press-conference venue — a useful signal of where Czech financial announcements are physically staged), Fotobanka/Videobanka. Infobanka is the route to historical full-text agency coverage that is not on the free web.

source_name: NEWTON Media – mediální archiv and PR Studio
why_relevant: The dominant Czech media-monitoring house. Its archive is advertised as covering press and online 'od roku 1989', i.e. deeper than any free web source, and it also operates PR Studio (press-release management/distribution) and Mediabase (journalist/influencer database). For this cell it is both a retrospective archive of how bank announcements were picked up and a competing distribution channel to ČTK Protext. Mediabase indirectly reveals which journalists cover Czech banking and payments.

source_name: Anopress IT – Czech media database
why_relevant: Long-standing Czech full-text media archive and monitoring provider, the main alternative to NEWTON Media for retrospective coverage of bank and payment-company announcements. Recorded here as a candidate to be re-verified: the fetch from this environment failed at the TLS layer, which is a transport-level failure, not evidence that the service is gone.

source_name: Monitora – media monitoring platform
why_relevant: Newer Czech/Slovak media-monitoring platform frequently used by mid-sized brands; relevant as a lower-cost route to tracking pickup of banking and payments press releases across Czech online media. Recorded as unverified — the fetch failed at the TLS layer from this environment.

source_name: MediaGuru – Czech media, marketing and PR trade news
why_relevant: Trade news site ('zpravodajský web o médiích, marketingu a reklamě', operated by PHD s.r.o.). Its /pr section reports on PR mandates, agency wins and campaign launches — which is how one learns that a given bank or payment company has changed its communications agency or is about to run a launch push. Also carries a media dictionary (medialni-slovnik) useful for building the Czech PR/media glossary.

source_name: Mediář – daily Czech media/marketing news and PR agency index
why_relevant: Independent daily (News Media s.r.o., editor Ondřej Aust) with dedicated /pr/ and /agentury/ sections listing dozens of Czech PR agencies. Snowballing the agency index identifies the intermediaries that write and place bank and payments press releases — a route to announcements that never reach a corporate newsroom, and a way to anticipate campaigns.

source_name: APRA – Asociace public relations (Czech PR agency association) member directory
why_relevant: Voluntary association of PR agencies operating in the Czech Republic, founded 1995, with a public directory of 26+ member agencies. Snowballing the member list yields the agencies whose client rosters and case studies name Czech banks, insurers and payment providers — an indirect but durable pointer to who announces what, and often to campaign material not present on corporate sites.

source_name: Komerční banka – Pro média / Tiskové zprávy
why_relevant: Newsroom of one of the three largest Czech banks and a PSE-listed issuer. Confirmed on fetch: three named press contacts, a directory of five in-house economists available for commentary (each with specialisation — a rare, directly useful expert map), recent releases dated August 2026 covering client numbers, fraud trends and macro forecasts, and a link to the press-release archive at /cs/o-bance/tiskove-zpravy. KB also pushes the same releases onto the ČTK Protext wire, so it is a good pair for measuring the newsroom-versus-wire lag.

source_name: Česká spořitelna – Pro média
why_relevant: Newsroom of the largest Czech retail bank (Erste Group). Confirmed on fetch: named spokesperson (Filip Hrubý) plus two press-centre officers with direct mobile numbers, and a stated scope of 'všechny kontakty, dokumenty a tiskové zprávy'. A dedicated media-contacts page exists at /cs/o-nas/pro-media/kontakty-pro-media. The press-release listing itself rendered as a shell on plain fetch, so it needs a browser-based collector.

source_name: Raiffeisenbank ČR – Informační servis / Pro média
why_relevant: Newsroom of a top-five Czech bank, notable for an unusual nested archive structure discovered by snowballing the homepage: press releases are foldered by year and apparently by sub-period, e.g. /informacni-servis/pro-media/tiskove-zpravy/tiskove-zpravy-2026/tiskove-zpravy-20268/. The site also exposes 'Povinně zveřejňované informace' and an investor-information page, so mandatory disclosure and PR are reachable from the same host. The obvious /o-nas/pro-media path 404s — the real path sits under 'informační servis'.

source_name: Fio banka – Média / Tiskové zprávy
why_relevant: Newsroom of an independent Czech bank/broker, with a two-track structure worth noting: 'tiskové zprávy' (formal releases) and a separate 'aktuality' stream that carries operational and security notices — the fraud/phishing warnings that never appear as formal press releases but are early indicators of payment-fraud trends. Item URLs carry a numeric id plus slug, e.g. /spolecnost-fio/media/tiskove-zpravy/327047-fio-banka-zavadi-bezpecnejsi-telefonicke-overeni.

source_name: ČSOB – Pro média (newsroom, bot-defended)
why_relevant: ČSOB is one of the largest Czech banking groups (KBC) and a major payments actor, so its newsroom is a must-have. Every path attempted on csob.cz returned HTTP 500 to this fetcher, which is characteristic of edge-level bot defence rather than a missing page — a 500 (not 404) means the host answered. Recorded as a live-but-blocked candidate; the exact newsroom path still needs confirmation from a real browser session.

source_name: UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia – corporate site / newsroom
why_relevant: Major CZ/SK cross-border bank whose Czech newsroom and mandatory-disclosure pages belong in the sweep. The root returned HTTP 403 to this fetcher — the standard signature of a WAF/bot filter on a live site, not a dead host. Newsroom path unconfirmed and deliberately not guessed here.

source_name: Banka CREDITAS – corporate site / newsroom
why_relevant: Fast-growing domestic Czech bank and an active acquirer, so its announcement flow matters for market-structure tracking. Root returned HTTP 403 to this fetcher — bot-defended-but-live. Newsroom path unconfirmed; CREDITAS releases are in any case visible on the ČTK Protext wire, which is the practical fallback for exactly this class of mid-sized domestic actor.

source_name: Burza cenných papírů Praha (Prague Stock Exchange) – Tiskové centrum a novinky
why_relevant: The exchange's own press centre and news stream, plus an events calendar (kalendar-udalosti) that pre-announces issuer reporting dates — a scheduling backbone for anticipating when Czech listed financials (Komerční banka, MONETA, Erste) will publish results. A burzovní newsletter signup exists. Note this covers exchange-level and issuer-facing announcements; the market-data pages are separate.

source_name: Patria.cz – Korporátní zprávy / Regulatory Announcements feed
why_relevant: Patria Online (part of the KBC/ČSOB orbit) runs the main Czech investment portal and republishes issuer regulatory announcements in a dedicated 'KORPORÁTNÍ ZPRÁVY' feed. For this cell it is the second distribution rail alongside ČTK: mandatory disclosures from listed Czech financials surface here in a single consolidated stream, often faster and in a more parseable form than on the issuer's own IR site.

source_name: KBC Group newsroom (parent-level distribution for ČSOB CZ)
why_relevant: Because csob.cz blocks automated access, the parent group's newsroom is the practical English-language substitute for group results and strategy items that cover the Czech business unit. Confirmed on fetch: 2026-dated releases including Q2 2026 results, PDF assets under /content/dam/kbccom/doc/newsroom/pressreleases/<year>/, and a press-release archive at /en/newsroom/press-release-archive/<year>/alle-onderwerpen.html. No Czech-specific releases were visible on the landing page, so treat it as a supplement, not a replacement, for the ČSOB CZ newsroom.

source_name: Erste Group – Press releases (parent-level distribution for Česká spořitelna)
why_relevant: Group-level press stream of Česká spořitelna's owner. Relevant because CEE-wide and capital/results announcements affecting the Czech subsidiary are frequently issued at group level in English before, or instead of, appearing on csas.cz. Fetch confirmed the press-releases page exists but returned only the header shell, so filters, date range, RSS and Czech-specific coverage are unverified.

source_name: Mastercard Europe newsroom – Czech edition
why_relevant: Card schemes announce Czech market data, product launches and partnerships through localised newsroom paths rather than through local corporate sites, which makes the /news/europe/cs-cz/ path the natural home for Mastercard's Czech press releases. The fetch returned HTTP 403 — bot defence on a live host — so the structure and content are unverified and the path should be reconfirmed from a browser.

source_name: Finance.cz – banking news and 'Komerční sdělení' (paid-PR) stream
why_relevant: Mass-market Czech financial portal (operated under the iinfo.cz group) covering taxes, banks, calculators and rates. For this cell its value is the clearly labelled 'Komerční sdělení' items interleaved with editorial content: these are paid placements by financial and insurance companies, so the stream reveals which institutions are actively pushing messaging and on what themes, distinct from formal press releases. No dedicated 'tiskové zprávy' section was visible.

source_name: Hospodářské noviny — Byznys (byznys.hn.cz)
why_relevant: HN is the Czech reference business daily (publisher Economia, a.s.). Its Byznys desk is normally first to interpret quarterly results of ČSOB, Komerční banka, Česká spořitelna, Moneta, Raiffeisenbank, Air Bank/Partners and to obtain executive comment and unpublished deal detail that never reaches a formal disclosure. Verified on fetch that corporate earnings items (e.g. Deutsche Telekom results, DAX 40 results, KKCG transactions) run in this section, confirming an earnings/deal beat.

source_name: Hospodářské noviny — Archiv (archiv.hn.cz)
why_relevant: Date-indexed archive of the HN print edition with search and purchasable PDF issues (observed price 40 Kč per issue). This is the retrospective entry point for reconstructing how a bank's results or a payments deal was reported at the time, including print-only analysis and charts that never appeared online.

source_name: Ekonom (týdeník, Economia) — ekonom.cz
why_relevant: Weekly business magazine from Economia (published since 1996), sister title of HN. Runs the longer-form 'why' behind a results season — sector profitability, branch/fee strategy, digital and payments strategy interviews with bank CEOs. Confirmed on fetch that Finance/Investment is a standing coverage area and that an issue archive exists at /vydani.

source_name: E15 — Finance a bankovnictví
why_relevant: E15 (publisher CZECH NEWS CENTER a.s., IČO 02346826) maintains an explicit, dedicated banking beat — verified on fetch: the section carries bank profits, interest rates, ČNB decisions, bank bond issues (e.g. Trinity Bank emissions), crypto adoption by banks and mortgage/fee topics. This is the single most on-target mainstream section in this cell for CZ bank earnings and payments news.

source_name: Euro.cz
why_relevant: Long-standing Czech business brand (originally the Euro weekly), now run online by the Internet Info / iinfo.cz group. Carries Byznys and Ekonomika desks, currency rates and investment/personal-finance coverage; useful as a second-opinion commentary channel on bank results and on unlisted banks. Note the editorial mix has drifted toward lifestyle/consumer topics, so precision is lower than HN/E15.

source_name: Seznam Zprávy — Byznys / Ekonomika
why_relevant: Seznam Zprávy (Seznam.cz) is the highest-reach Czech-owned digital newsroom with a well-resourced investigative/business desk. It breaks ownership, governance and deal stories about banks and payment firms that listed disclosures omit, and it covers unlisted institutions. Section tree verified on fetch (Byznys 194 with Finance 299, Firmy 297, Reality 298, Právo 308 subsections).

source_name: Seznam Zprávy — Finance (sekce 299)
why_relevant: The finance sub-desk of Seznam Zprávy, self-described as 'Investování, burzy a trhy, daně a důchody'. Verified on fetch that it carries corporate/bank result items (e.g. a piece on the world's oldest bank defending itself against a takeover, Lego profit) alongside pensions, markets and crypto — a clean single URL to watch for results-season interpretation.
